thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: high token-queue depth observed on prod-us-west inference fleet. p95 latency up ~2.3x, throughput down ~30% vs baseline. Alert group: inference.queue.depth > 8k for 5m. Link: https://observability.redwood.example/alert/4445550000 :rotating_light:
oncall-olivia: I'm paged, looking. Any recent deploys?
sre-marc: no deploys in last 2 hours. seeing elevated KV eviction rates and a spike in small-sequence traffic from two customers.
eng-runtime-lina: checking runtime metrics — KV hit rate dropped from 98% -> 72%. CPU on kvproxy pods ~85%.
oncall-olivia: good catch. can we confirm whether routing fallback kicked earlier?
sre-marc: routing logs show some traffic routed to cheaper-quantized variants, but backpressure queued on token-queue due to small batch inefficiencies.
eng-runtime-lina: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase kvproxy replicas + raise memory limits 2) enable prefix caching for hot customers 3) route high-concurrency tenants to dedicated pool (if available) 4) short-term autoscale up GPUs in us-west.
oncall-olivia: start with 1 + 4. Marc, can you scale kvproxy to +2 replicas and bump mem for current pods?
sre-marc: scaling now. kubectl patch deployment/kvproxy -n prod --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":4}}' then rolling restart. Increasing VM autoscale trigger threshold to prefer adding nodes earlier.
incident-bot: Change executed by sre-marc: scaled kvproxy -> 4 replicas.
eng-runtime-lina: while that's rolling, I'll opt-in prefix caching for top-5 tenants causing churn: enabling cache rules for tenant IDs 742, 1291, 2010.
pm-jasper: heads-up — CS will need a customer-facing note if we expect >30m disruption.
cs-amy: please share a short status blurb I can use for customer comms and status page.
oncall-olivia: draft status page update below (short):
```
Status: Degraded performance in US-West inference (partial throughput reduction)
Impact: Some requests experience higher latency and lower token throughput. Affected customers: subset of high-concurrency tenants routed through shared pool.
Mitigation: We scaled KV proxy and increased autoscale responsiveness. Prefix caching enabled for top tenants. Additional capacity being provisioned.
ETA: 15-30 minutes for steady recovery; follow-up update in 15 minutes.
```
cs-amy: LGTM, can you also provide a customer email snippet for enterprise accounts?
oncall-olivia: customer email draft: 
```
Hi —
We detected and mitigated a performance degradation affecting inference in our US-West region starting at <time>. Some requests experienced increased latency and reduced throughput. We have scaled internal proxy components, enabled targeted caching for the most impacted tenants, and provisioned additional capacity. Expected recovery: within 15–30 minutes.
If you see ongoing issues, please reply to this thread or contact support@redwood.example.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Operations
```
eng-runtime-lina: after kvproxy scale finished, p95 dropped from 2.3x -> 1.4x, token queues reduced by ~55%. Still higher than baseline but improving.
sre-marc: autoscale is adding 2 GPU nodes, ETA ~6min.
pm-jasper: I'll prepare an internal one-pager for stakeholders summarizing impact and mitigations.
cs-amy: sending the customer note now to affected enterprise contacts.
incident-bot: Status page updated (draft posted) by oncall-olivia.
eng-runtime-lina: FYI, tracing shows a small traffic fan-in pattern from tenant 742 due to retry storms — we're throttling retries at edge to reduce load.
oncall-olivia: good. Lina, can you handoff to next on-call in 20m if still in recovery? I'll remain until steady.
sre-marc: metrics look stable, token queue still trending down. continue monitoring.
oncall-olivia: Handoff plan if still active at +20m: oncall-miguel will take over. Steps: 1) validate kvproxy health 2) check autoscale progress 3) confirm p95 <= 1.2x baseline or escalate to SRE lead.
oncall-olivia: Closing note: if recovery completes earlier I'll post final status; otherwise Miguel please pick up. :white_check_mark:
